profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21721 Filigree Court, Suite B, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC11 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
Equinix DC11 is a 116,831-square-foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's multi-building Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. The operator publishes no power capacity, square footage specifications, certifications, or cabinet density figures for DC11 itself. Equinix's representative DC2 specification on the same campus lists 4 kVA minimum cabinet density and N+1 power and cooling redundancy, but these are not confirmed for DC11.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley holds roughly 10 million square feet of data center space, described as the greatest concentration on the planet and anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's late-1990s DC1 and DC2 buildings. The campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 operators have published power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts.

Without published power capacity for DC11, the facility cannot be ranked among Virginia's disclosed sources of AI compute infrastructure. The campus itself ranks 24th in Virginia by published megawatts, but this rank reflects only Equinix's other disclosed Ashburn buildings, not DC11's contribution. Whether DC11 matters to AI scaling depends on figures Equinix has not published.
